The appendix of Block Diffusion RooflinesPrevious: 11 · Conclusion

Every number in Parts 1–7 is a roofline bound computed from a cost model, not a measurement; Parts 8–11 give the measurements. This appendix describes the exact accounting behind the maps, the headline numbers and the calculator, points to the measurements that check it, and lists the sources of the model shapes and accelerator specifications.

Exact accounting

The maps, headline numbers and calculator do not use Proposition 1. They evaluate every pass of a generation: AR prefill and \(G-1\) decode steps; TD encoder prefill, then per canvas \(S\) bidirectional denoising passes and one causal commit. Each pass counts:

  • FLOPs: linear layers; exact (query, key) pairs under causal, bidirectional and sliding-window masks, in-canvas keys included; the LM head on every logit position; for DiffusionGemma, the self-conditioning soft embedding and MLP.
  • Bytes: weights with \(U(N)\) experts; the vocabulary matrix once per use; KV reads and writes; activations under a fused kernel schedule (or none, when on-chip); logits and probabilities, \(\lambda\) times per output position.
  • Decoder ratio: a denoising pass multiplies every per-layer term (FLOPs, weights, KV reads, activations) by \(r\); its vocabulary and self-conditioning terms are unchanged. For \(r \gt 1\) the memory footprint adds \((r-1)L\) layers of weights.
  • Time: the per-pass roofline, \(\max(F/\pi, Q/\beta)\), or, under the calculator's kernel-by-kernel rule, the sum of that roofline over the kernel classes (dense layers, experts, global, window and sparse attention, indexer, vocabulary head). The class sums equal the totals exactly.

The closed forms for masked key counts match brute-force counting. Proposition 1 matches this accounting to within 1.32% without vocabulary (Table 3). Model shapes come from each checkpoint's config.json; for DiffusionGemma also from its safetensors headers (25.25B text parameters, 3.08B active per token plus a 0.74B head).

Check against measurement

Parts 8–11 compare these bounds with throughput measured in vLLM 0.28.0 on one H200, with every kernel attributed to a component. An earlier check in this appendix (84% of the bound at batch 1, 34% at batch 64) used stock vLLM, whose CUDA graphs read stale causal flags (Part 9), against bounds under independent routing; it is superseded by Part 11.

Source and updates

The cost model is the BDModel script in /assets/roofline/note.js, which every chapter loads. Last updated 15 November 2026: an introduction; Parts 8–11 on measurements in vLLM on one H200; the sparse-attention index cache corrected to one key per token.

Sources

Models: google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it (config and safetensors headers) and the config.json of each preset on Hugging Face. Forward pass and self-conditioning: transformers modular_diffusion_gemma.py. Sampler: DiffusionGemma docs. Hardware: vendor datasheets and documentation, including Google TPU7x, TPU v6e and the AMD MI325X datasheet; figures marked ≈ are derived or disputed. Roofline: Williams, Waterman and Patterson, "Roofline: an insightful visual performance model", CACM 2009. Block diffusion: Arriola et al., "Block Diffusion", ICLR 2025. Measurements (Parts 8–11): vLLM 0.28.0 and the roofscope harness on one H200 SXM; related work is listed in Part 11.
